# Tumbling Windows — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Tumbling Windows. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-23 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Periodic per-key sensor summaries are a practical Atlas pattern: group measurements inside each window and compute averages, minima and maxima. A public smart-grid demo uses daily tumbling windows, while MongoDB's tutorial illustrates minute-scale rollups. (medium confidence) — https://dev.to/mongodb/aggregate-streaming-data-within-windows-of-time-using-atlas-stream-processing-1lm1 · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://github.com/ramonfnasc12/smart-grid-kafka-atlas

## Structure and components

- [statement] For event-time tumbling windows, interval duration alone does not establish wall-clock output latency. Watermark progress controls closure, and allowedLateness delays closure relative to that watermark while permitting newer windows to open. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-tumbling.md · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture.md
- [statement] Non-overlap describes window membership. It does not establish exactly-once end-to-end delivery, guarantee inclusion of arbitrarily late events, or guarantee an output every interval of wall-clock time. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/windows.md · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture.md, https://scotty.stream/paper/verwiebe_vldbj2023.pdf

## How it works

- [statement] Atlas supports event-time and processing-time boundaries. Event time uses document timing; processing time uses the server clock when the processor consumes a document. A delayed event can therefore fall into different windows under the two modes. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-tumbling.md · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture.md
- [statement] An idle source can leave an event-time window waiting for watermark progress. Atlas provides idleTimeout to allow windows to close during source inactivity; the stage reference and architecture guide disagree about exactly when its timer begins. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-tumbling.md · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Atlas defaults boundary to eventTime. When boundary is processingTime, idleTimeout and allowedLateness cannot be configured. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-tumbling.md · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture.md
- [statement] A record that arrives after its Atlas window closes cannot be assumed to update that aggregate. MongoDB documents routing late-arriving documents to a dead letter queue when one is configured. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/windows.md · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] With a Kafka source, Atlas waits for all partitions to pass the watermark. An idle partition can prevent windows from closing or producing results; the architecture guide recommends the source option partitionIdleTimeout. This differs from the window-level idleTimeout option. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture.md · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://github.com/mongodb/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/mongodb-atlas-stream-processing/references/output-diagnostics.md
- [statement] Atlas supports only one window stage per stream processor pipeline, and a single $group key inside a window has a documented limit of 100 megabytes of RAM. These are Atlas implementation limits rather than properties of the tumbling-window model. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-tumbling.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Tumbling windows partition time into fixed-duration, contiguous intervals without overlap. Each event timestamp maps to one interval; this describes assignment, not a guarantee that arbitrarily late events will be accepted. MongoDB, Apache Spark, and Confluent independently document this window model. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/windows.md · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/streaming/apis-on-dataframes-and-datasets.html, https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/ksqldb/concepts/time-and-windows-in-ksqldb-queries.html, https://scotty.stream/paper/verwiebe_vldbj2023.pdf
- [statement] In Atlas Stream Processing, $tumblingWindow supplies a finite set of streaming documents to its nested aggregation pipeline. This enables per-interval grouping and statistics such as averages, minima, and maxima. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-tumbling.md · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/windows.md, https://dev.to/mongodb/aggregate-streaming-data-within-windows-of-time-using-atlas-stream-processing-1lm1
- [statement] The Atlas $tumblingWindow stage requires interval and pipeline. interval.size is a positive integer, and interval.unit accepts ms, second, minute, hour, or day. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-tumbling.md
- [statement] Atlas aligns tumbling boundaries to UTC by default and offers offset to shift them. An offset of eight hours moves the boundaries eight hours ahead of UTC; the documentation does not establish automatic daylight-saving adjustment. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-tumbling.md
- [statement] The documented default allowedLateness is 3 seconds, and zero can be supplied explicitly. This is a window-closure allowance relative to watermark progress, not a promise to include every delayed record. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-tumbling.md
- [statement] Late events do not move the fixed time boundaries of a tumbling window. They can change its aggregate if accepted while its state is retained; Atlas allowedLateness delays closure to allow this. (high confidence) — https://scotty.stream/paper/verwiebe_vldbj2023.pdf · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture.md
- [statement] Atlas preserves stateful window processing through checkpoints. After interruption, a processor resumes from its last committed checkpoint; this does not establish end-to-end exactly-once delivery to every possible sink. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-tumbling.md · keywords: Tumbling Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture.md
